pluss::note::full¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::full(integer_range sizes, string_view value)

Fill A Known Shape With One Repeated String¶

full() is the shape-first constructor: you already know the geometry you want, and you want every cell to start life holding the same string. It allocates a Note of shape sizes and writes value into all numel cells.

Reach for it when the shape comes from somewhere other than the text — a column count fixed by a schema, a grid whose dimensions are computed, a placeholder block you will overwrite cell by cell later. It is the text counterpart of pluss::series::full and pluss::timeline::full: same argument order (shape, then fill), same “allocate and broadcast one value” contract.

sizes is any contiguous range of std::int64_t. Its length is the rank and its entries are the extents:

  • an empty range → a rank-0 scalar (one cell)

  • {n} → a rank-1 column of n cells

  • {r, c} → a rank-2 block

  • {a, b, c} → a rank-3 block

The result is always UTF-8 mode (encoding=utf8); value is stored verbatim in every cell, with no trimming or re-encoding. For a bytes-mode fill, there is no free-standing full_bytes — build the shape from an existing Note with full_bytes_like, or pass an explicit sizes list to bytes.

Relationship to empty and rep¶

  • empty(sizes) is exactly full(sizes, "") — a shape filled with the empty string.

  • rep(value, sizes) is full with the arguments swapped to value-first, plus an initializer_list overload so rep("-", {5}) needs no RangeView wrapper. Use rep when the value is the point of the call and the shape is a small literal; use full when the shape is the point.

Shape rules¶

Every extent must be non-negative; a zero extent is allowed and yields a Note with no cells but a retained shape. Rank may not exceed three. Shape is validated before any allocation.

Example 1: Fill A Matrix With A Placeholder¶

std::array<std::int64_t, 2> sizes{2, 3};
const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::full(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes), "TODO");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["TODO", "TODO", "TODO"], 
  ["TODO", "TODO", "TODO"]
]

Every cell holds the same string; the shape came entirely from sizes.

Example 2: An Empty sizes Range Produces A Scalar¶

std::array<std::int64_t, 0> sizes{};
const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::full(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes), "x");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[], dim=0, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
"x"

Rank 0, one cell — the same scalar a bare pluss::note::make("x") builds, just reached shape-first.

Example 3: A Zero Extent Is Legal¶

std::array<std::int64_t, 1> sizes{0};
const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::full(
    pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes), "x");
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

The Note has no cells but keeps its rank-1 shape — a valid, typed empty column, distinct from a scalar holding "".

Example 4: A Rank Above Three Is Rejected¶

std::array<std::int64_t, 4> sizes{2, 2, 2, 2};
try {
  pluss::note::full(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes), "x");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

Note supports up to 3D

Example 5: A Negative Extent Is Rejected¶

std::array<std::int64_t, 1> sizes{-1};
try {
  pluss::note::full(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Of<std::int64_t>(sizes), "x");
} catch (const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string msg(e.what());
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

sizes must be non-negative

Validation happens before allocation.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::empty: full(sizes, "") — a shape of empty strings.

  • pluss::note::rep: the value-first spelling, with an initializer_list shape overload.

  • pluss::note::full_like: take the shape from an existing Note instead of a sizes list.

  • pluss::note::make: build from the text itself when the shape is implied by the data.
